fluff.overview: The Banzai is a ninety-ton experimental assault BattleMech developed in 3076 by Luthien Armor Works at their New Samarkand facility for the Draconis Combine. Born from a radical redesign of the Mauler chassis, the Banzai represents the same philosophy of transformative engineering that produced the Hatamoto-Chi from the Charger, taking an existing platform and reshaping it so thoroughly that the result is considered an entirely new design. Conceived during the desperate fighting of the Jihad, the Banzai was intended to serve as a heavy assault platform incorporating both Inner Sphere experimental systems and captured Clan weaponry. Only four prototypes were ever constructed, marking it as one of the rarest experimental designs to emerge from the Combine's wartime development programs.
fluff.capabilities:
The Banzai retains only the Mauler's endo steel skeleton from its parent design, building an entirely new machine around that frame. A massive 360-rated extralight fusion engine, augmented by both MASC and a supercharger, gives the ninety-ton assault 'Mech a base speed of 64 km/h with the ability to reach bursts of 100 km/h, a remarkable feat for a machine of its tonnage. Seventeen and a half tons of standard armor provide exceptional protection, allowing the Banzai to absorb punishing fire as it closes with its targets.

The weapons loadout reflects the design's close-combat philosophy. Paired Clan-manufactured large pulse lasers in the right arm deliver devastating accuracy at speed, supported by two Clan medium pulse lasers and a head-mounted Clan ER small laser. A large vibroblade in the left arm gives the Banzai fearsome melee capability. The most distinctive feature is the integrated booby trap, an explosive self-destruct device tied to multiple critical systems that ensures the 'Mech's destruction if captured or critically damaged, denying salvage to the enemy at the cost of everything in the blast radius. A full-head ejection system provides the pilot a chance of surviving such an event, though the margins are slim.

The Banzai's fifteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load adequately under normal combat conditions, though simultaneous activation of the vibroblade and energy weapons places significant strain on heat management. The reliance on captured Clan pulse laser systems and multiple experimental components makes the design extremely difficult to maintain and repair, a critical weakness that sharply limits its operational availability.
fluff.history:
The Banzai emerged from the crucible of the Jihad, when Luthien Armor Works engineer Mariella Irabu was tasked with upgrading the Daboku with newly available technologies. Finding the base MAL-1K chassis too constrained for her vision, Irabu retained only the endo steel skeleton and designed an entirely new assault 'Mech around it. The project, which began in 3076, incorporated both Inner Sphere experimental systems and captured Clan weaponry, proof of the Combine's willingness to embrace unconventional solutions during the desperate fighting against the Word of Blake.

Only four prototypes were completed before the end of the Jihad. The first operational Banzai was assigned to the Eighth Dieron Regulars and accompanied that unit during the liberation of Dieron from Word of Blake occupation. The prototype participated in the assault on the Blakist-held prefecture capital, where it demonstrated both the terrifying potential and inherent risks of the design. After engaging Blakist forces and sustaining heavy damage, the 'Mech's engine was breached during withdrawal, triggering the full-head ejection system and subsequently the booby trap. The resulting explosion destroyed surrounding Blakist forces but also caught friendly Combine troops in the blast. The pilot did not survive the rough landing of the ejection system.

Despite the loss, BattleROM analysis confirmed the design's combat effectiveness, validating the engineering decisions that went into the Banzai. The remaining three prototypes were retained for further testing and potential combat deployment. The Banzai's extreme maintenance requirements, reliance on captured Clan components, and the controversial booby trap system have limited enthusiasm for full-scale production. Yet, the design stands as evidence of the innovative (if ruthless) engineering philosophy that characterized Combine weapons development during the Jihad era, and the three surviving prototypes await dedicated testing or future combat assignments.
fluff.deployment: This variant is the sole configuration of the Banzai to reach prototype stage. The original design concept called for capacitor-augmented ER PPCs, but the lead engineer elected to replace these with Clan pulse lasers to better complement the 'Mech's high-speed attack profile, trading raw damage potential for accuracy on the move. All four prototypes were built in this configuration, with no subsequent variants attempted due to the limited production run and the Jihad's end.
